title: refactor(sim): the camcraft-sim CLI simulates through Stock on the field engine
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #595** (issue #585), which adds `Columns::cell()`. Merge #595 first. This is M7.3 step 5 of 6 (#26).

The `camcraft-sim` headless CLI built a `Dexel` block and called the column engine's `simulate` directly.
- **Now:** it builds `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, …)`, runs `Stock::simulate`, and reads removed volume, cut cells and lowest cut column by column through `Stock::columns()` (`Columns::cell`/`nx`/`ny`/`top_at`).
- **No-verdict columns:** a field column with no verdict (NaN) counts as uncut, the same abstention every `Columns` consumer makes.
- **Result:** no `Dexel` remains in the binary.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/588-cli-on-stock.md`.

## Readings: identical output before and after

I recorded the binary's full output on 5 golden programs × 2 tool diameters, before (column engine) and after (field engine): `crates/app/tests/golden/<file>.cl` with box `-60 -60 -25 60 60 0`. **Every line matched**, including the exit code and verdict.

## What changed

The contributor asked for this: PathPilot Hub simulates Tormach's lathes, and CamCraft shipped only a generic `lathe.mch`. This adds two shipped lathe machines from **Tormach's operator manuals**, which the contributor supplied:

| | Tormach 8L (UM10753 §3.1) | Tormach 15L Slant-PRO (UM10225 §1.1) |
|---|---|---|
| X / Z stroke | 4.5" / 10" | 10" / 12" |
| Spindle | 180-2500 / 350-5000 rpm (two ranges, 5C) | 180-2500 rpm (6" chuck) |
| Feed / rapid | 150 IPM | 60 IPM |
| Power | 1.1 kW (1.5 hp, Tormach web; the manual states none) | 2.24 kW (3 hp continuous) |
| Tools | 99 (gang / QCTP, PathPilot tool table) | 8 (8-position turret) |

- **Conventions:** both machines are inch, `kind: lathe`, with the full stroke either way of the work zero, like the shipped Tormach mills.
- **Conservative choices:**
  - **8L X is 4.5":** the manual settles it. Tormach's web knowledge base says 10", which is the 15L's figure.
  - **15L top speed is 2500 rpm,** the default chuck's rating. A shop on the 5C collet (250-3500 rpm) can raise it in its own copy.
- **Test updates:** the shipped-machine expectation list (`machine.rs`) names both lathes. The Tormach Z0 safe-retract law (`tormach_safe_retract.rs`) is a mill-post law, so it skips lathes; they retract on their own post (#612).
- **Not included:** the 15LX (#619) and the M+ mills (#618) follow separately.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/611-tormach-lathes.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/tormach_lathes.rs`, 2/2:** every lathe states its manual's figures (travel, feed, rpm and ranges, power, tool count, kind lathe, inch, no Y). The lathes are never offered as mills.

- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the app suites are green after this fix (the first run caught the two machine-list tests). conformance 6, posting 17, lathe_post 7, turning_thread 8.
- **`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`:** clean.
- No golden or snapshot changed. Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## Not exercised

A Hub run on the 8L or 15L. Until #612 (the PathPilot lathe post) lands, these machines judge envelope, rpm and feed, but the default lathe post writes Fanuc dialect, which PathPilot won't run.

title: fix(ui): GPU tests fall back to the hardware adapter and say when they skip
body:
## What changed
Every GPU test, and the real `--headless` run, requested `force_fallback_adapter: true`, a software adapter. Metal has none. So on every Mac:
- `gpu_render`, `trace_composite` and `trace_parity` silently skipped and reported **pass**;
- `headless_run_succeeds` and the two headless CLI tests **failed** with "No suitable graphics adapter found".

New `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`:
- **`device()`:** tries the software adapter first (deterministic CI on Linux/Windows), then the default hardware adapter. It returns the device, queue, which kind it got and the adapter's name and backend. If both fail, the error names both reasons.
- **`device_for_test(suite)`:** prints the adapter it renders on. With no adapter it prints a loud `*** <suite>: SKIPPED (no adapter) - NOT a pass ***`, and `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns that into a failure.
- **Headless app path:** `headless::run` (shell.rs) now uses the helper, so the CLI tests are fixed through the app path itself.
- **Not an `#[ignore]` lane:** that would drop these ~1 s suites from quick and batch everywhere. Reasoning in `docs/decisions/615-gpu-adapter.md`.

## How tested (on a real Apple M3 Max, Metal)
| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| gpu_render (9) | 9 silent skips | 9 rendered, pass |
| trace_composite (4) | 4 silent skips | 4 rendered, pass |
| trace_parity (5) | 5 silent skips | 5 rendered, pass |
| `headless_run_succeeds` | FAIL | pass (Metal) |
| the two headless CLI tests | FAIL | pass |

- **Totals:** 0 of 21 before, 21 of 21 after.
- **Stability:** three parallel runs in a row pass, and so does `trace_parity` with `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`.
- **No tolerance changes:** every coverage, parity and depth assertion holds on hardware. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- **Clippy:** clean.
- **Not exercised:** the skip path itself, because this Mac always finds an adapter, and Linux/Windows runs.

Changelog: On macOS the GPU tests and the headless run fall back to the hardware (Metal) adapter, and a GPU test with no adapter prints a loud SKIP (CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1 turns it into a failure) (#615)

Fixes #615

title: fix(ui): orthographic view casts parallel rays for the traced stock and vertex-pick visibility
body:
Two Orthographic-view follow-ups found while fixing #600 (that depth fix is carried by #604). This branch is off main and doesn't depend on #604; its tests check the ray and camera math on the CPU.

## #609: the traced stock casts parallel rays in ortho (`7b9800d1`)
- **`PreviewCamera`** (sim `stock_sim/preview.rs`):
  - a new `ortho_half_height: Option<f64>`;
  - `orthographic(h)`, which refuses a non-finite or non-positive half height by name;
  - `ray(px, py, w, h) -> (origin, dir)`. In ortho, each pixel's ray starts on the eye plane and runs along the view direction, matching `Camera::mvp` and `ray_through`. Perspective is unchanged.
- **Who uses the same rule:** the CPU march, the GPU march (`trace.wgsl`, via the unused `world_lo.w`) and the compositor (`composite.wgsl`, via `frame.z`).
- **Viewport wiring:** `eye_geom::preview_camera` takes the half height from the viewport camera, and the cache key includes it, so switching modes re-traces.

## #610: vertex-pick visibility in ortho (`4d9922b1`)
- `vertex_pick::sight_origin`: perspective starts at the eye as before. Ortho starts at the corner's own point on the eye plane, so the test runs back along the view direction, as `ray_through` does.
- A corner at or behind the eye plane is not offered.

## How tested
- **sim `stock_preview::an_orthographic_eye_casts_parallel_rays_from_its_view_plane`:** parallel rays from the eye plane, the box top at one depth, misses off the footprint, perspective unchanged, and a bad half height refused.
- **ui `trace::eye_geom::tests::the_traced_stock_lands_on_the_mesh_pixel_in_both_projections`:** all 8 corners of a stock box, projected through `Camera::mvp`, lie on their pixel's traced ray in both projections. With the fix reverted, a corner misses by 2.81 against a pixel width of 0.80.
- **ui `vertex_pick_tests::orthographic_visibility_runs_along_the_view_direction_not_to_the_eye`:** an occluder on the parallel ray hides a corner, and an occluder only on the line to the eye doesn't. The old test got both backwards.
- **Gate:** ui lib 378, stock_preview 11, gpu_render, trace_composite and trace_parity pass. Clippy is clean (ui, sim, app).
- **Shaders:** both pass naga 30.0.1's parser and validator. **This machine has no wgpu adapter, so the GPU and compositor paths weren't exercised; a review on a machine with an adapter should run gpu_render, trace_composite and trace_parity.**

Changelog: Orthographic view: the traced stock sim view now casts parallel rays, so it lines up with the ortho-drawn part, meshes and toolpaths (#609)
Changelog: Orthographic view: vertex picking tests visibility along the parallel view direction, so a hidden corner is no longer offered and a visible one is no longer refused (#610)

Fixes #609

title: test(ui): structural tests no longer race on the live theme table
body:
## What changed
`structural::shell_structure_light` and `shell_structure_dark` failed intermittently in parallel ui runs (#605).
- **Cause:** the live theme table `theme::LIVE` (read through `theme::current()`) is one per process. The structural and snapshot tests already serialise on `snapshot_guard()`, but `tests/theme_door.rs::the_theme_door_switches_the_theme_and_undo_restores_it` drives the real light → undo → redo → undo frame-edge sync without that lock, so it flips the shared table in the middle of a structural test.
  - A flip to dark breaks `shell_structure_light` ("frame-edge sync rode the world's reference").
  - A flip to light breaks `_dark`.
- **Fix (tests only):** the theme-door switch test takes `snapshot_guard()`, and the `SNAPSHOT_LOCK` doc says any test whose frames move the world's theme must take it too.
- **Why not per-harness:** the table is process-wide by design, read at ~44 sites with no `State` to hand. Making it per-harness would be a large production change for a race that exists only in tests.

## How tested
- **Before:** 30 parallel runs of `egui_app::tests::` gave 5/30 failures, all `shell_structure_light`. With the theme-door test skipped, 0/30, which confirmed the cause.
- **After:** 0/30 on those runs, and 20 full parallel `camcraft-ui --lib` runs gave 0 structural or other failures. The headless-GPU test fails only on this machine.
- Clippy is clean.

Changelog: none (test-only)

Fixes #605

title: fix(ui): orthographic view maps depth to wgpu's 0..1 so the scene draws
body:
## What changed
Clicking **Orthographic** blanked the viewport (#600, reported with a headless repro: perspective painted 9,326 px, ortho 0).
- **Root cause:** `Camera::mvp`'s ortho branch (`crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`) used OpenGL's depth row (−1..1), but WebGPU keeps clip z only in 0..w. With ortho's w = 1, everything nearer than (near+far)/2, about 20× the orbit distance, was clipped.
- **Fix:** `[2][2] = 1/(near−far)`, `[3][2] = near/(near−far)`, so near maps to 0, far to 1, linear in between. The depth test (`Less` against a 1.0 clear) is unchanged.
- **Unchanged:**
  - Perspective, which survives with positive w.
  - Picking, `dolly_cursor`, `vertex_pick` and the overlays, which use only x/y/w.
  - The traced-stock composite, which already assumed the WebGPU range.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/600-ortho-depth.md`. The ortho near plane stays at the eye plane, which keeps the #434 pick-ray laws, and the perspective row is left alone.

## How tested
- **New unit test:** `projection_tests::ortho_depth_spans_wgpus_zero_to_one_clip_range`. Near → 0, far → 1, midpoint → 0.5, and the target plane lies between them. It failed before the fix ("near maps to 0, got -1").
- **New GPU test:** `gpu_render::ortho_box_stock_paints_like_perspective`, the issue's repro: ortho paints more than half of perspective's pixels. **It skips on this machine (no GPU adapter)**, so it needs a GPU run, or a hands-on check of clicking Orthographic.
- **Gate:** ui lib 377 passes; the headless-GPU test fails only on this machine. Clippy is clean.

## Found, not fixed (follow-ups)
- The traced-stock sim view always casts perspective rays, so in ortho it won't line up with the meshes.
- `vertex_pick`'s ortho visibility check tests along the line to the eye point, not the parallel view direction.

Changelog: Orthographic projection draws the scene again: its depth now maps to WebGPU's 0..1 clip range instead of OpenGL's -1..1, which clipped the whole model (#600)

Fixes #600

title: fix(ui): orthographic depth maps into WebGPU's clip volume, not OpenGL's
body:
The ortho branch of `Camera::mvp` mapped depth the way OpenGL's `glOrtho` does - NDC z over [-1, +1]. WebGPU's clip volume wants `0 <= z <= w`, and the ortho matrix holds `clip.w == 1` (the #434 law tests pin that), so every point nearer than `(near + far) / 2` was clipped away before rasterization. With `far = 40 * dist`, that cut plane sits twenty times the orbit distance out: everything in view, so clicking **Orthographic** blanked the viewport.

Perspective carries the same OpenGL-style z row but `clip.w` is the eye distance there, which keeps clip z positive beyond ~0.2 mm - far closer than the camera can orbit - so perspective was unaffected.

## The change

The ortho z row (`viewport.rs`, the `[col][row]` proj literal) becomes

```rust
[0.0, 0.0, 1.0 / (near - far), 0.0],
[0.0, 0.0, near / (near - far), 1.0],
```

near maps to 0.0, far to 1.0, and ortho depth is now linear. The depth attachment already clears to 1.0 under `CompareFunction::Less`, so no pipeline or shader change is needed. The x/y rows already speak WebGPU and are untouched, as is the perspective branch (its z quirk costs depth precision, not geometry - out of scope here).

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `law_tests::projection_tests::the_ortho_depth_spans_zero_to_one_between_the_planes` - depth at the near plane, the far plane, and strictly between with monotonic climb. On main: "the near plane sits at -1".
- `gpu_render::orthographic_paints_the_band_perspective_does` - the stock box from `box_stock_paints_steel_over_background` under `test_cam()`, painted in both modes, with the same band bounds and a comparability check (each within 1.5x of the other). On main: 0/65536 pixels.

## Tested

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` builds clean.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 378 passed, 5 ignored.
- `--test gpu_render`: 10 passed (9 existing + the new one).
- `--test trace_composite`: 4 passed (its first run hit the known pre-existing fallback-device crash race; clean on rerun, and it only exercises the untouched perspective path).

Changelog: orthographic view no longer blanks the viewport - the parallel depth row maps into WebGPU's clip volume (#600)

Fixes #600

title: fix(ui): the setup page's lay-on-plane controls stay on screen, so a picked face is turned flat
body:
**Stacked on #593** (#555), which is on #573 (#557 + #554). It includes their commits until they merge.

## Root cause of the reopened #330
The turn itself was never broken. `pick::lay_on_plane` / `AlignPartToSetup` turn a picked tilted face onto G17/G18/G19 on main, and a new app test pins that. What was broken is what a user could reach on the Setups page. Reproduced through the real shell (1280×720, the block turned 30° about X, real viewport clicks):
1. **Edge snapping (main):** the plane row armed Edge mode (`plane_pick.rs:31`), so a click on the tilted face took an edge, `check_lay` refused it, and Apply stayed grey. **Already fixed by #573** (7d641c8b, #554: the plane row picks faces only).
2. **Controls off screen (main and the stack):** the face row was one long line. In the ~285 px properties pane, **Flip, "Face to plane level" and Apply fell past the right edge**, so clicks on them did nothing. The only Apply in reach was the Part alignment row's angle Apply, which turns about the bounds centre. That matches the report's "it only moves the model". Without a reachable Flip, the default also lays the face's outside up, with the part below the plane.

## What changed
- **Face row:** split into short lines: label + "Pick a face"; plane + Flip; "Face to plane level"; the picked face; then **Apply face** on its own line.
- **Other rows:** the three-points row (#555) and the "Axes in the plane" rows (#557) overflowed the same way and got the same treatment.
- **Not used:** `horizontal_wrapped`, which didn't work because other rows widen the pane's content.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/330-face-lay-rotate.md`.
- **Maintainer's call:** the default Flip is unchanged: unflipped means the face's outside points along +axis, so a face picked on G17 lays "outside up". Many users will expect the picked face to become the bottom, so flipping the default may be worth it.
- **Not addressed:** the Part alignment row's angle Apply turning about the bounds centre (the "shifts relative to the origin" part of the report). Follow-up or maintainer's call.

## How tested
- **New UI real-click test:** `plane_face_lay::a_clicked_tilted_face_is_turned_flat_onto_g17_not_only_moved`.
  - It clicks Pick a face → the tilted face in the viewport, asserts Flip, "Face to plane level" and Apply face are on screen, then clicks Flip → Apply face.
  - Result: face normal −Z, face at Z 0, part above. Ctrl+Z restores.
  - It fails on main (an edge is taken) and on the stack without the layout fix (the Apply click misses).
- **Structural:** `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` asserts every option of the face, points and axes rows is inside the window.
- **App:** `plane_align::a_tilted_face_is_turned_flat_onto_each_plane_with_the_part_above_it` covers G17/G18/G19 with undo. It passes on main too, which pins that the command was right.
- **Gate:** plane_align, plane_align_edges, points_align, axis_align, setup_align, winding_align, commands_undo and ui lib 385 pass. The headless-GPU test fails only on this machine. Clippy is clean.

Changelog: Setups page "Lay on a plane": Flip, "Face to plane level" and the row's own "Apply face" stay on screen in the properties pane (they ran off its edge), so a picked tilted face can be laid flat on G17/G18/G19; the three-points and axes rows get the same fix (#330)

Fixes #330

title: feat(mcp): an idle live-session client is dropped after a timeout
body:
**Stacked on #474** (#183, MCP live in the GUI). It includes #474's commits until that PR merges.

## What changed
The live listener (`crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`) serves one client at a time, and a silent local connection held the session until it hung up.
- **Idle window:** a new `IDLE_TIMEOUT` of 5 minutes. A client that sends no complete line for that long gets one `notifications/message` warning and is disconnected. The log names it (`client <peer> dropped: idle - …; serving the next client`), and the next client is served.
- **What counts as idle:** the clock restarts after each answered line. Time spent answering doesn't count, and a partial line doesn't reset it. Windows shorter than the 50 ms poll step are raised to it.
- **Constructor:** `Inbox::listen_with_idle(port, wake, idle)` is new. `Inbox::listen` uses the default, so the GUI caller is unchanged.
- **Kept from #474:** the JSON-lines-only rule, the `MAX_LINE` read cap, the 5 s write timeout and stop/join on drop.
- **Not done:** a new client replacing an idle one, because it would let any local process kick a live agent off between calls. The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/567-mcp-idle-timeout.md`.

## How tested
- `mcp_live::an_idle_client_is_dropped_by_name_and_the_next_one_is_served` (300 ms window): a silent client gets the note and then EOF, not early, and the log names it. A second client is served afterwards.
- `mcp_live::a_client_that_keeps_talking_is_never_dropped_as_idle`: eight pings 150 ms apart, all answered.
- **Before the change:** the idle test fails with the window forced back to 5 minutes.
- **Gate:** app `mcp_live` 9 and ui `mcp_live` 2 pass; clippy (app and ui, `-D warnings`) is clean.

Changelog: The live MCP listener drops a client that sends nothing for 5 minutes, telling it why and logging its address, so the next agent can connect (#567)

Fixes #567

title: feat(post): probing hooks for the Haas, Mazak and Siemens posts
body:
**Replaces #360** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #333** (`issue/257-gcode-comments`, which touches every `.cps` post). This diff includes #333's commits until it merges; the #173 work itself is the last commit. Review #333 first.

## What changed
- **`haas.cps`: probes.** It adds `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult`:
  - G31 skip; #5061–#5063 trip read; no-contact and out-of-tolerance alarms through `#3000`;
  - incremental G91 back-off;
  - `G10 L2 P` from `#5221+20×slot`, or a `#3006` operator stop.
  - Source: the Haas Mill Operator's Manual (public).
- **`mazak.cps`: probes.** The same macro-B contract in Mazak EIA/ISO words:
  - `IF[..]GOTO` with unique N labels, since `IF..THEN` is not documented on every EIA generation;
  - the operator stop is a comment plus M00.
  - Source: Mazak's EIA/ISO programming manual (Fanuc-compatible).
- **`sinumerik.cps`: probes.**
  - `MEAS=1 G1`; `$AC_MEA[1]` checks for no contact; `$AA_MW[..]` reads the trip into R50–R61.
  - `IF..ENDIF` + `MSG` + `SETAL` + `M0` alarms; incremental G91 back-off.
  - Sets the offset through `$P_UIFR[..,TR]` (FI copied when the frame changes), then re-selects the active G5x.
  - It refuses by name to set G58/G59 (axial offsets on an 840D) or to work from an offset outside G54–G57 / G505–G599.
  - Source: SINUMERIK 840D sl Programming Manual (Fundamentals / Job Planning).
- **`heidenhain.cps`: still refused by name.** The TNC 640 ISO manual this post follows documents no skip move and no trip-position variable; TNC probing lives in the separate touch-probe-cycles manual. The script now carries a comment saying so, and the existing engine refusal is pinned.
- **Spindle at 0 rpm.** Haas, Mazak and Siemens no longer write a spindle-on block at 0 rpm (a touch probe), as fanuc already did. No existing golden contained `S0`.
- `docs/decisions/173-probe-hooks-dialects.md` names every source and judgement call.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_dialects.rs` (7 tests): bore-centre goldens `golden/nc/{haas,mazak,sinumerik}/probe_bore_centre.nc` (G55 set from G54), both operator-stop variants, the Sinumerik G59 refusal, and the Heidenhain refusal.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): post suites ok. App suites: everything passes except `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag`. That test pins `PROJECT_VERSION == 51`, but main is now at 53, so it fails the same way on `upstream/main`; PR #345 fixes it. This commit touches no Rust source.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **No controller or simulator run yet**, so this stays a draft. The posted words follow the public manuals only.
  - Mazak is the weakest-sourced: its `#5061` / `#5221` numbering should be confirmed against a Mazak manual.
  - Sinumerik's MEAS/`$AA_MW` path needs a check on a real 840D or a simulator.
- **The probe is not armed by the post.** Arming is machine-specific and stated by no stream record. An unarmed probe never trips, so it raises the no-contact alarm, which matches fanuc.

Changelog: The Haas, Mazak and Siemens 840D posts write the Probe operation (skip move, trip read, tolerance alarm, set work offset); Heidenhain keeps a named refusal (#173)

Fixes #173

title: fix(post): judge the tool-number clash per machine
body:
**Replaces #440**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so #440 can no longer be updated. **Now stacked on #471** (the replacement for #439).

(Originally stacked on #439.) The #438 work is 9d9ac93d.

## What changed
- **The tool-number clash check (#221) is judged per machine.** `tool_numbers::clash_per_machine` runs the existing `clash()` on each machine group from `program_mounts(world, false)`. `posting::op_streams` calls it, which covers per-op files too.
- **Why per machine, not per NC file:** a T number names a pocket in one machine's tool changer.
  - Two machines have two tool tables, so T2 on each is fine.
  - Two posts on one machine still load from one carousel, so a shared number there is still refused.
  - Grouping per file (machine plus post) would let that real clash through, so I rejected it.
- **Messages:** a single-machine program gets the exact #221 message, unchanged. A multi-machine refusal starts with the mount's label (`Setup1 (machine, post): tools '…' and '…' would both post as T3 …`).
- The rationale is in `docs/decisions/388-per-setup-mount.md` (#438 section).

## How tested
- New `setup_mounts_post::a_tool_number_shared_across_machines_posts_but_clashes_within_one`:
  - across machines: a mill tool numbered 2 and the lathe's T2 post as two files;
  - within one machine: a clash is refused, naming both tools, the T number and Setup1, and not the lathe tool.
- `tool_numbers::two_tools_posting_one_number_refuse_by_name` (single machine) is unchanged and passes.
- `setup_mounts_post` 6/6, `setup_mount` 6/6, `tool_numbers` 6/6, `posting` 17/17, `post_not_judged` 4/4. `clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: The tool-number clash is judged per machine, so two machines in one program may each use the same T number (#438)

Fixes #438
